discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 200935
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
535 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and pleasant weather persists through the entire week with
  highs either side of 70, lows in the 40s, and no rain until
  next week at the earliest.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 126 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

Upper flow across area east of the Rockies is relatively weak as mid 
level ridging and a couple surface high pressure centers pair to 
keep the area dry. As the first high pressure center moves into 
southeast Canada from the Northern Great Lakes, a backdoor cold 
front sets up east of MI and north of OH, which may be able to 
advect marine air into our east potentially setting them up for 
morning fog Wed AM. Another northern stream wave and trailing 
surface high pass by to the north of the area Wed through Thu time 
frame. Because the front washes out across the area Wed night, 
minimal lowering of temps occurs for Friday (from mid 60s to low 70s 
Thu to low to upper 60s Fri). With the mid level ridging still 
staunchly in place across the Plains States and Mississippi Valley, 
troughing in the west struggles to advance eastward and surface lows 
take a north-northeasterly track into Southcentral Canada. So, it 
could be until the first part of the next work week before we 
get our next rain into the area. There are hints that the mid 
level ridge finally pushes eastward at this time and this helps 
some combination of a diving wave within the northern stream and
some southern stream moisture to make it up this way to provide
rain.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 533 AM EDT Tue Oct 20 2026

Surface high pressure over the Northern Great Lakes pushing east 
pairs with mid level ridging to quell rain chances during the taf 
period. This pattern allows prevailing east winds through the bulk 
of this period. A few hours of patchy fog will be possible this
morning, but appears to be staying away from the terminals. As 
a backdoor front settles east of MI and north of OH, hi- res 
guidance is producing advection fog that could affect FWA Wed 
AM. Will project SBN stays out of the fog in this taf issuance. 
Otherwise, expect VFR conditions prevail through the rest of 
the taf period.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller
AVIATION...Roller

spc.text:
SPC AC 201230

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0730 AM CDT Tue Oct 20 2026

   Valid 201300Z - 211200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Organized severe thunderstorms appear unlikely through tonight.

   ...Great Basin into the Southwest and Southern/Central Plains...
   Isolated showers and thunderstorms ongoing this morning across parts
   of southern/central NM may develop downstream today over portions of
   the southern/central Plains as modest southwesterly mid-level flow
   persists. As a closed mid/upper-level low digs southward off the
   West Coast, convection capable of producing occasional lightning is
   also forecast to develop this afternoon through tonight across parts
   of the Great Basin and Southwest. Low-level moisture is forecast to
   further increase through the period over the lower CO River Valley
   and southern/central AZ.

   While a stronger thunderstorm or two may develop across southeast AZ
   this afternoon with daytime heating aided by orographic effects,
   better large-scale ascent associated with a strong southwesterly
   mid/upper-level jet will likely be delayed until late tonight/early
   Wednesday morning. Greater coverage of thunderstorms may be realized
   towards the end of the period across central/northern AZ, but in a
   weak thermodynamic environment. The overall severe hail/wind threat
   across the Southwest currently appears lower and even more isolated
   than yesterday, so have not introduced any severe probabilities with
   this update.

   ..Gleason/Kerr.. 10/20/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 200558

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1258 AM CDT Tue Oct 20 2026

   Valid 211200Z - 221200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF
   CENTRAL INTO EASTERN ARIZONA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe hail/wind and perhaps a tornado may occur over portions of
   Arizona, southern Utah and western New Mexico on Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid-level trough will move ashore through the day Wednesday,
   promoting large-scale ascent of a moistening airmass across the
   Desert Southwest to the Four Corners region. Scattered thunderstorms
   are expected over these regions, and given the anticipated overlap
   of marginal to moderate buoyancy with a highly sheared airmass, a
   few severe thunderstorms are possible.

   ...Desert Southwest to the Four Corners...
   Marginal instability should develop through the day, primarily
   driven by increasing low-level warm-air and moisture advection
   (given ample cloud cover expected). Surface dewpoints should
   increase into the 60s F, especially over central AZ, yielding over
   1500 J/kg MLCAPE given 7+ C/km mid-level lapse rates. A 50-70 kt
   southwesterly 500 mb jet will overspread the warm sector and
   accompanying southeasterly antecedent flow, yielding elongated
   hodographs with sizeable low-level curvature. Supercell
   thunderstorms are expected by late afternoon, accompanied by a
   severe wind and hail threat. Given the size of the low-level
   hodographs, a tornado or two may also occur.

   ...Central to southern CA Shoreline...
   The core of an 80 kt 500 mb jet will overspread central and southern
   CA during the later half of the period (00-12Z Thursday), resulting
   in relatively straight but highly elongated hodographs. During this
   time frame, a moist marine airmass will advect to the CA shoreline
   while being overspread by 6.5-7 C/km mid-level lapse rates, yielding
   250-500 J/kg of short and thin MLCAPE. Given the scant buoyancy,
   convection should be low-topped, with short line segments and
   supercell modes possible. A damaging gust or two is the main threat
   with any stronger storm that can reach the shore, as well as a
   landfalling waterspout.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/20/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 200730

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0230 AM CDT Tue Oct 20 2026

   Valid 221200Z - 231200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF THE
   DESERT SOUTHWEST INTO THE GREAT BASIN...

   ...SUMMARY...
   At least isolated severe wind/hail producing storms are possible
   across portions of the Great Basin into the Desert Southwest on
   Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid-level longwave trough will overspread the CONUS west of the
   Rockies on Thursday, resulting in the continued northward advection
   of a moist, marginally unstable low-level airmass across the Desert
   Southwest into the Great Basin. A broad 50-70 kt mid-level jet will
   overspread these regions during the day, resulting in strong
   vertical wind shear, that coupled with the marginal instability will
   yield scattered strong to severe thunderstorms.

   ...Desert Southwest into the Great Basin...
   The aforementioned 50-70 kt southwesterly 500 mb jet streak will
   overspread south-southeasterly low-level flow, resulting in
   elongated hodographs and over 50 kts of effective bulk shear. Though
   widespread clouds may inhibit surface heating to some degree,
   continued low-level moisture advection (e.g. 60+ F surface
   dewpoints) beneath 7+ C/km mid-level lapse rates will yield up to
   1000 J/kg MLCAPE. Such conditions will favor multicells and
   supercells capable of producing at least isolated instances of
   severe hail and/or wind and perhaps a tornado. A marginal risk has
   been introduced to address the severe threat. However, if areas of
   locally greater surface heating (i.e. breaks in clouds) become
   evident, then higher severe probabilities may be needed in future
   outlooks.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/20/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
